digest: A finance workstation (WS-FIN-09) was compromised via a phishing attachment, leading to the execution of an encoded PowerShell script. This script initiated command and control (C2) beaconing to a known malicious domain (stage2.malicious-domain.xyz) and IP (198.51.100.44) over TLS. The C2 domain is associated with Fast Flux DNS and has a high malicious reputation. Network isolation of the affected host has been approved.

evidence_findings.title: Initial Execution via Phishing Attachment
evidence_findings.subject: WS-FIN-09
evidence_findings.evidence: excel.exe spawned powershell.exe with a hidden, encoded command line: powershell.exe -NonI -W Hidden -EncodedCommand <BASE64_PAYLOAD>. This activity was detected on host WS-FIN-09 (IP 10.20.4.115).
evidence_findings.conclusion: An initial compromise occurred on WS-FIN-09, likely via a phishing attachment, leading to the execution of a malicious PowerShell script.

evidence_findings.title: Encoded PowerShell Decoded to C2 Download
evidence_findings.subject: PowerShell command
evidence_findings.evidence: Analysis of the encoded PowerShell command revealed an attempt to download content using IEX Net.WebClient from a remote stage2 domain.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The encoded PowerShell was used to evade detection and establish further communication with an attacker-controlled domain.

evidence_findings.title: Outbound Command and Control (C2) Beaconing
evidence_findings.subject: 10.20.4.115 to 198.51.100.44
evidence_findings.evidence: Host 10.20.4.115 (WS-FIN-09) established a persistent TLS session (450s duration with 30-second interval pulses) to 198.51.100.44 on port 443. This traffic is identified as C2 beaconing.
evidence_findings.conclusion: WS-FIN-09 is actively communicating with an external C2 server.

evidence_findings.title: Malicious C2 Domain Identified
evidence_findings.subject: stage2.malicious-domain.xyz
evidence_findings.evidence: The destination domain stage2.malicious-domain.xyz (resolving to 198.51.100.44) is identified as malicious, uses Fast Flux DNS, and has a reputation score of 89/100. It also matches a US-CERT advisory bulletin.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The C2 infrastructure is confirmed to be malicious and associated with known threat activity.

evidence_findings.title: Host Network Isolation Approved
evidence_findings.subject: WS-FIN-09
evidence_findings.evidence: Network isolation for host WS-FIN-09 was approved by the SOC Lead at 2026-08-14T18:25:30.000Z.
evidence_findings.conclusion: Initial containment measures are being implemented to prevent further compromise or data exfiltration.

attack_chain.description: Phishing delivery mechanism, likely an attachment, led to the initial compromise of WS-FIN-09.
A user opened a malicious attachment, causing excel.exe to spawn powershell.exe with an encoded command.
The use of an encoded PowerShell command was an attempt to bypass security controls and obfuscate malicious intent.
The PowerShell script initiated a download from a remote domain and established persistent C2 beaconing to stage2.malicious-domain.xyz (198.51.100.44) over TLS.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Persistent TLS session with periodic pulses observed.
Encoded PowerShell payload deobfuscated, revealing C2 download attempt.
Threat intelligence confirms C2 domain as malicious.

ioc_indicators.context: Command and Control (C2) beaconing domain, identified as malicious and using Fast Flux DNS.
C2 server IP address, destination for outbound beacon traffic from WS-FIN-09.
Malicious PowerShell command executed on WS-FIN-09, used for defense evasion and C2 initiation.
Internal IP address of the compromised host WS-FIN-09.

remediations.description: Isolate host WS-FIN-09 (IP 10.20.4.115) from the network to prevent further C2 communication and lateral movement.
Block stage2.malicious-domain.xyz and 198.51.100.44 at network perimeter devices (firewall, proxy, DNS) to prevent further C2 activity and protect other assets.
Conduct a full forensic analysis of WS-FIN-09 to identify the initial infection vector, persistence mechanisms, and any further compromise.
Remove any malicious files or persistence mechanisms found on WS-FIN-09.
Restore WS-FIN-09 from a clean backup or reimage the system after forensic analysis.
Review security awareness training for users, especially regarding phishing attachments, and enhance endpoint detection rules for encoded PowerShell commands.

unknowns: The full decoded content of the Base64 payload beyond the IEX Net.WebClient download attempt.
The specific details of the initial phishing email (sender, subject, attachment name).
Whether any data exfiltration occurred during the C2 session.
The full extent of the compromise, including potential lateral movement or other affected systems.
The specific variant of Cobalt Strike or other malware used.
